blocks.text: Source: The Match Factory / Goodfellas
‘Fatherland’, ‘La Bola Negra’

Pawel Pawlikowski’s Fatherland and Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s La Bola Negra lead the nominations for the 2026 European Film Awards (EFAs), announced today at Thessaloniki International Film Festival.

Fatherland , a monochrome drama about the relationship between writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, was nominated in the most categories with 11. Its nominations included European film, and director, screenwriter and editor for Pawlikowski, with Henk Handloegten and Piotr Wojcik also nominated in the latter two categories respectively.

blocks.text: The Mubi film premiered in Competition at Cannes in May, where Pawlikowski shared the best director prize with Calvo and Ambrossi.

Their La Bola Negra received 10 EFA nominations, including for European film, director, and screenwriter (with Alberto Conejero). The film is an epic tale of queer love in 20th-century Spain, set across three time periods and inspired by the unfinished last work of the playwright Federico Garcia Lorca.
Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or winner Fjord took five nominations, including European film, director, and screenwriter.

Acting nominations include Sandra Huller, nominated twice in European actress for Fatherland and Rose ; Fjord duo Renate Reinsve and Sebastian Stan in European actress and actor respectively; and real-life partners Penelope Cruz and Javier Bardem, nominated for Bunker and The Beloved respectively.

The European Animation Film category includes Olivier Clert’s Lucy Lost and Sebastien Laudenbach’s Viva Carmen ; while Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s Venice title NAZA is among the European Documentary nominees.

All five nominees in the animation and documentary categories were also all nominated for European Film, meaning some of the fancied fiction titles including Minotaur , Elsinore , Everytime and Gentle Monster didn’t make the final list of 15 nominees in that category (although all were nominated in other categories).

France-based Palestinian actress Hiam Abbass has already been announced as the recipient of the European Achievement in World Cinema honorary award, while previously announced nominees for the European Young Audience Award include Louis Clichy’s animation Iron Boy .
The nominations are based on the votes of 5,700 members of the European Film Academy. The winners will be unveiled at the awards ceremony in Athens, Greece on January 16.
Joachim Trier’s Sentimental Value led the winners for the 2025 awards, with six prizes including best film; just ahead of Oliver Laxe’s Sirat , which took five awards.
